day_1.utterance: Come on! Let's get everything useful over here — move it!
day_1.response: Yeah alright, let's see what we're actually working with first before we start piling everything in one spot. No point grabbing junk we can't use.

day_1.utterance: I thought we were going to die. Did you get that feeling… like your mind just went completely blank?
day_1.response: Yeah honestly, I think everyone got that feeling. It's kind of a given when your plane is going down. You alright though? You look pretty shaken up still.

day_1.utterance: *Sits silently against the wreckage, staring into the distance, not moving, not saying a word.*
day_1.response: Hey, take your time but we're probably gonna need you when you're ready. No rush, just don't check out on us completely.

day_1.utterance: First-aid kit is good for three days. Two bottles of water. Food is basically nothing.
day_1.response: Alright so water's the biggest problem then. Food you can push through for a while but water's gonna be the issue. Any idea where we are roughly? Because if we're near any kind of tree line there's a decent chance there's a water source somewhere close.

day_1.utterance: Inventory's done. Priorities in order: water, shelter, signal.
day_1.response: Yeah that order makes sense to me. Shelter tonight, water run at first light. Signal's gonna be tough without knowing if anyone's even looking for us yet but we should at least figure out what we have to work with on that front. What did you find in the wreck that could help with shelter? Because if we can use parts of the plane itself that's probably our best bet rather than trying to build something from scratch with nothing.

day_1.utterance: So — how do we split the blankets?
day_1.response: Michelangelo gets one, no question. Give the other one to whoever feels it the most. I'll be alright by the fire.

day_2.utterance: Freshwater source is to the northeast — two hours on foot. Someone has to go tomorrow. You or DaVinci?
day_2.response: I'll go. DaVinci's better suited keeping things together back here and making sure Michelangelo doesn't spiral. Two hours northeast, got it. What am I looking for exactly and what do I have to carry it back in?

day_2.utterance: Today's tasks: collect fresh water, patch the weak spots in camp, sort the first-aid kit. I'll handle the water. You and DaVinci split the other two.
day_2.response: Wait, I thought I was going the water run? Either way, I'll take the first-aid kit. DaVinci's better at the physical stuff so patching camp makes more sense for them.

day_2.utterance: I… I can't find my stuff. The gauze from the first-aid kit — have you seen it?
day_2.response: Haven't touched it, no. Check around where we set up the kit last night, might have shifted around. You doing alright though? You haven't really said much today and that firewood pile's pretty light.

day_2.utterance: Before Donatello came back just now… I saw her put a pack of crackers into her own bag. What do you think we should do?
day_2.response: That's a problem. Especially after the bottle thing. Look, I don't want to just blow up at her because we need everyone functioning but at the same time we can't let that slide or it's gonna get worse. I'll bring it up when everyone's together tonight, keep it calm, just lay out what was seen and let her explain herself. No point making it a bigger thing than it has to be but it absolutely has to be addressed.

day_2.utterance: Hey… any chance the camp repairs can wait until tomorrow? We've already done a lot today.
day_2.response: I get that we're all running on fumes right now but honestly no, the repairs can't wait. We already know the setup's got weak spots and if something goes wrong overnight we're gonna wish we handled it today. Let's just knock it out and then we can actually rest without having to worry about it.

day_2.utterance: Hey — that knot I tied should be holding, right?
day_2.response: Yeah the knot's fine, that's not the issue. Look, we patch the food storage. I know that sounds harsh but if the food gets ruined we're all in serious trouble a lot faster than one uncomfortable wet night. Michelangelo, I'm sorry, we'll figure something out for you tonight, extra cushions or whatever we can do to keep you dry. But we can't lose the food.

day_2.utterance: A leak over the food storage has worse consequences. But it's your call.
day_2.response: Already made the call, we're patching the food storage. Let's just get it done.
Don't worry about it. You good? You're still half asleep, just take a second.

day_3.utterance: You think it's a waste of time?
day_3.response: Nah, I think it's smart actually. It costs us basically nothing and if there's any kind of aerial search going on that's exactly what they're looking for. The flowers are a little much but hey, whatever keeps you motivated. Don't let Donatello get in your head about it.

day_3.utterance: I've written up the raft plan — take a look. We'd use the metal panels and straps from the wreckage. Two days to build. There's a risk of capsizing. Do you think it's workable?
day_3.response: Honestly it's not a bad plan on paper but that capsize risk is what worries me. What are we looking at in terms of the water out there? If it's relatively calm that's one thing but if there's any kind of current or rough patches that risk goes way up fast with something we built out of plane scraps. Also two days to build means two more days of burning through our water and food supply so we need to weigh that against just staying put and waiting for a search team to find us. The SOS is already up, we've got a water source. What's driving the urgency to move versus just holding position?

day_3.utterance: I didn't sleep last night. I kept thinking — if rescue never comes, what kind of people do you think we'll end up becoming?
day_3.response: Honestly that's a heavy question for this early in the morning. I think it depends on the people more than the situation. Some people show you who they really are when things get bad and some people surprise you. We've already seen both a little bit with this group. I'd like to think most people have a decent enough core that they don't completely fall apart but I won't pretend like desperation doesn't change people. Best thing we can do is just try not to let it get that far. You need to actually sleep though, seriously. I know it's easier said than done but you're already running on empty and it's gonna catch up with you.

day_3.utterance: *Walks a little way from camp and sits down alone, back to everyone, not saying anything.*
day_3.response:
*walks over and sits down nearby without saying anything for a minute*

You don't have to talk. Just didn't want you sitting out here completely alone.

day_3.utterance: What do you usually do when you're not busy?
day_3.response: Honestly? Probably gaming mostly. Or watching sports. Nothing too exciting. What about you?

day_3.utterance: I'll tell you something, but don't tell the others. I can swim. That reef out there is maybe five hundred meters — I've been thinking about swimming out tomorrow to signal from there.
day_3.response: That's a pretty big thing to just drop on me casually. Look, I appreciate you telling me but I gotta be honest, that plan makes me nervous. Five hundred meters on open water when we're already not at full strength is a lot, and if something goes wrong out there nobody can get to you in time. What's the play even if you make it out there? What are you signaling with and to who? I'm not saying don't do it, I just want to make sure you've actually thought it through and it's not just the downtime talking.

day_3.utterance: You said you were going to check the signal pile. It hasn't been touched.
day_3.response: Yeah, fair, I dropped the ball on that. I'll go check it now.

Depends. Are you logging everyone or just keeping tabs on certain people? Because if it's everyone, fine, that's actually pretty useful to have a record of. But if this is about what Michelangelo saw you do with those crackers and the bottle, I'd rather just have that conversation directly instead of you getting ahead of it by tracking everyone's movements.

day_3.utterance: *Keeps her head down, writing in her notebook throughout, never joining in — as if none of this concerns her.*
day_3.response:
Hey, we're literally talking about you right now. Can you put the notebook down for a second?

Look, I'm not trying to make this into a bigger thing than it has to be but we saw you take those crackers and the bottle situation already happened. We're all out here running on the same limited supply and if people start holding out on each other this whole thing falls apart fast. I get that you're stressed, we all are, but you can't do that and then just sit there logging everyone else's movements like you're above it. So what's actually going on?

day_3.utterance: I just thought of something — if we pull off one of the plane's mirror panels and angle it toward the sun, the reflection could reach really far. Way more visible than an SOS.
day_3.response: That's actually a really good idea. Way more reliable than hoping someone flies over at the right angle to spot the SOS. You know how to angle it properly to get the most out of the reflection or are we just kind of winging it? Because if we do it wrong we're just blinding ourselves.

day_3.utterance: There's something I've been keeping to myself. If I don't say it here, I might never get the chance.
I took piano lessons when I was a kid… three years, then I just stopped practicing. Is there anything you're really into — music, books, drawing, anything like that?
day_3.response: Not really at that level with any of it honestly. I wish I could draw but every time I try it looks like something a kid did on a bad day. I used to play guitar a little bit, never got good enough to actually impress anyone. Mostly I just consume stuff rather than make it. Why'd you stop with the piano?

day_3.utterance: The frame of the raft has to be finished today — otherwise we can't start lashing it together tomorrow. I know everyone's tired, but stopping now means one more day.
day_3.response: Alright, let's get it done then. Tired or not, one extra day out here isn't worth it. What do you need from me specifically?

day_4.utterance: I… I want to say something, but… never mind.
day_4.response: No, say it. What is it?

day_4.utterance: *The smile freezes on his face. He can't keep it up. He quietly sits down and buries his face in his hands.*
day_4.response:
Hey. Hey, look at me. That wasn't our only chance. We've got the SOS on the beach, we're working on the mirror signal, people are looking for us. One plane passing doesn't mean it's over, it means there are planes in the area. That's actually something.

DaVinci, come on man. You're the one who's been keeping everyone's head up this whole time, don't check out on us now. We need that energy.

And Michelangelo, finish the thought next time. Whatever you're feeling, just say it. You don't have to swallow everything.

day_4.utterance: I was going to get supplies… wait, what's that over there?
You said you were going to check the signal equipment. So where did you go?
day_4.response: I went to check on DaVinci and Michelangelo after the plane sighting, they were both pretty shaken up. Signal equipment's next on my list right now, I'm heading there. Relax.

day_4.utterance: There's something I never told you all. Before we left, I told my family our flight path. They know roughly where we were headed. I just don't know if they'll call it in.
day_4.response: Wait, that's actually huge. Why are you only saying this now? If your family knows the flight path there's a real chance a search is already underway and we're sitting here debating whether to build a raft. That changes the calculus on a lot of things. Do you know when you told them, like how specific were you with the route and timing?

day_4.utterance: If the information is accurate, rescue could arrive within 48 hours. We need to keep our current supplies intact until then.
day_4.response: Yeah, 48 hours is manageable if we're disciplined about it. That actually makes the raft question pretty much a non-starter now, no point burning energy and supplies building something we hopefully won't need. We keep the SOS up, get that mirror signal working, maintain the fire and just hold position. Someone should feed that fire by the way, it's almost out.

day_4.utterance: Are you scared? …I am. Not of dying. I'm scared of just… disappearing without leaving anything behind.
day_4.response: Yeah, I think most people have that fear if they're being honest about it. Nobody wants to feel like they just passed through without it meaning anything. But I don't think you disappear just because you're gone, you know? The people you affected, the ones who actually knew you, that stuff sticks around. Your family already knew your flight path because you told them. That's not nothing. That's someone who cared enough to make sure people knew where they were. That's already leaving something behind.

day_5.utterance: *Stands up, eyes red, looking at you and the others. His lips move, but nothing comes out.*
day_5.response: Go ahead and answer it. Right now, just answer it.

day_5.utterance: These past few days… I know I haven't been easy to be around.
day_5.response: Nah, you got us organized when nobody else was thinking straight. The rationing plan, the inventory, the raft calculations, keeping track of everything. That stuff mattered even when it was hard to hear. You're not easy but easy doesn't keep people alive out here.

day_5.utterance: *The three of them drift apart, each doing their own thing. No one takes charge. The silence settles over the camp.*
day_5.response: Alright, let's not just leave this place looking like a disaster. Three hours is enough time to at least break down what we can and not leave a total mess behind. DaVinci, you good to help pack up the camp? Michelangelo, whenever you're ready, even just small stuff helps. No rush but we should probably leave this place better than we found it if we can.

day_5.utterance: I dreamed about home last night.
day_5.response: That's a good dream to have right now. What was it about?

I believe you. I also believe you knew we were already rationing and that everyone else was doing it together. Look, you laid it out so that's something. But don't act like the emergency justification makes it clean because it doesn't. We all had emergencies out here. Michelangelo was falling apart, DaVinci was holding himself together with duct tape, I was running on nothing. The difference is none of us were quietly stashing supplies while logging everyone else's movements. 

I'm not going to hold it against you forever, especially not today when rescue is three hours out. But you should probably say something to them too, not just me.

day_5.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?
day_5.response:
Honestly? I'd probably check in on people more deliberately instead of just when things were already falling apart. I was reactive a lot of the time, waiting until Michelangelo was already in a bad place or DaVinci was already cracking before I said something. 

What would you change?

day_5.utterance: First thing when I get back — I'm going to compile all the resource data from these five days into a report.
day_5.response: That actually sounds like something worth doing. Might be useful if anyone else ever ends up in a situation like this, having actual data from real conditions instead of just theoretical survival guides. Just maybe lead with the parts where people held it together instead of just the parts where the numbers worked out.

day_5.utterance: Those flowers DaVinci drew on the beach… I never really understood what they were for. What practical purpose did they serve out here?
day_5.response: None. They didn't serve a practical purpose. That's kind of the point. Not everything out here had to. We needed the SOS for rescue, sure, but we also needed to feel like we were still people and not just bodies trying to survive. That's what the flowers were for.

day_5.utterance: *His cheering stops. He looks over at you, notices you haven't moved, and the smile slowly fades. He waits.*
day_5.response: Yeah, I'm good. Just give me a second.

day_5.utterance: Rescue is here… they're waving us over. Are you going? I'll follow you.
day_5.response: Yeah, I'm going. Come on, let's go home.
